If that query returns zero rows (e.g., embed_category unset/blank or not matching a category name), `[0]` is nil and indexing `['id']` will raise, crashing the migration before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:15 — Fallback reads uncategorized_category_id with [0]['value'], but that row only exists if the setting was overridden, so the migration crashes on an empty result.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration blindly indexes SQL results with [0] (e.g., `execute(...)[0]['id']` for `embed_category` and later `execute("SELECT value ... uncategorized_category_id")[0]['value']`) without checking that the query returned any rows. If either SELECT returns an empty result set, `[0]` is nil and the migration will raise (NoMethodError). The finding’s specific claim about when `uncategorized_category_id` exists in `site_settings` isn’t provable from the diff, but the unchecked empty-result crash risk is verifiable in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Host values are put straight into the INSERT SQL without quoting, so an apostrophe breaks the migration and crafted setting values can inject SQL.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If `h` contains an apostrophe it will break the SQL, and because it is unescaped interpolation of data read from `site_settings` (`embeddable_hosts`), a crafted value could inject arbitrary SQL during migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:22 — The backfill copies raw lines without stripping http(s):// prefixes, paths, whitespace/CR, or blank lines, so migrated rows don't match the new lower(host) lookup and some are empty hosts.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the backfill inserts rows via raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` for each `h` from `val.split("\n")`. This bypasses the EmbeddableHost model’s `before_validation` normalization (stripping http/https and paths) and any format validations, so values like `http://example.com`, `https://example.com/123`, trailing `\r`, whitespace, or blank lines can be persisted as-is (empty string is allowed by the DB `null: false`). Later lookups use `record_for_host` -> `URI(url).host` and `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, which will not match entries stored with schemes/paths/CR, causing migrated allowed-hosts to stop working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Old site settings are deleted inside a reversible change method, so a rollback drops the new table and loses the embedding host and category config for good.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration is written as `def change` (which Rails treats as reversible for things like `create_table`), but it also runs irreversible SQL, including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. On rollback, Rails will drop the new `embeddable_hosts` table (reversing `create_table`), but the deleted rows in `site_settings` will not be restored, causing permanent loss of the previous embedding host/category configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:4 — host has no index (lower(host) or unique), so the per-request embed lookup does a full table scan and duplicate hosts are allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — The lookup lowercases only the stored column, not the incoming referer host, so mixed-case referers are wrongly rejected.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, the query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, but the incoming `host` value is set from `uri.host` without being downcased. If the referer URL contains a mixed-case hostname (or if `uri.host` preserves case), the RHS parameter won't match the `lower(host)` LHS, causing legitimate hosts to be rejected. The diff also doesn't normalize stored host to lowercase (only strips scheme/path), so case mismatches are possible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Validation accepts a ":port" suffix that is kept in the stored host, but matching uses uri.host without the port, so port-scoped entries never match and admins may think a port restriction is enforced.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the validation regex allows an optional ":port" suffix, and the before_validation hook strips scheme and path but does not strip the port, so a saved record can remain like "example.com:3000". However, matching in record_for_host parses the incoming URL with URI(...) and uses uri.host (host without port) for the lookup: where("lower(host) = ?", host). This means port-qualified stored hosts will never match, so admins could believe a port restriction is enforced when it is not/doesn't work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:7 — The allow-list only holds bare hostnames with no path or port scoping, so any page on an allowed host (e.g. user-content paths on shared hosts) can embed and create topics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24 — category_id is not checked against existing categories, so admins can point embeds at a nonexistent category and topic creation will fail or produce orphaned topics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:15 — update/destroy do not handle a missing record or missing params (nil host), which raises 500 errors instead of 404/400.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — record_for_host compares lower(host) to an un-downcased uri.host and ignores stored ports; no test covers mixed-case hosts or host:port entries, so the regression goes undetected

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, record_for_host does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` after setting `host = uri.host`. `uri.host` is not downcased, so for mixed-case referers (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com`) the SQL becomes `lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com'`, which will not match a lowercased stored host in a case-sensitive DB.
